shill: routing_table: Replace per-table route on receipt of main table route Previously, routes added to the main routing table would simply be removed if shill is aware of a corresponding entry existing in the per-device table. This change modifies such behavior to have these entries replaced instead. This prevents a potential scenario in which a default route fails to be added to a per-device table but shill believes it to be there, leading to the inability for future route additions to actually make their way from the main routing table to the per device table. This also allows for the 'expires' property to be used by routes in per-device tables in the future, as periodic routes added by the kernel would be able to update the expiration time. BUG=chromium:941597 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -v6 RA entries getting updated upon receipt of new RA (tested by adding an expire value to existing default routes in per-device tables, which shill itself doesn't do). Change-Id: I52d4b8de6ace4a36e02822537ef7eb7cf7b7d936 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1672252 Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org>

shill: connection: Avoid unnecessary table free/alloc when updating IPConfig Previously, shill would always free and allocate a table ID in Connection::UpdateFromIPConfig. Prior to using per-device tables for physical interfaces, this caused no issues, as the result was essentially a no-op. With physical per-device tables, however, this causes us to actually clear out all of the existing routes. Since the passed-in IPConfig does *not* currently contain all IP configuration information, the remaining information may indeed be lost. As Device generally prefers an IPv4 config, this manifests itself as the loss of v6 routes, including any dhcpcd-addded routes. In most cases, this situation will eventually resolve itself upon the reception of a v6 RA, but the frequency of such events is not consistent between environments and is certainly not frequent enough to rely on for continued connectivity. Moreover, such behavior is not RFC 4861 compliant. Since UpdateFromIPConfig is triggered by DHCP events, a DHCP renewal (for v4 or v6) can cause this undesired behavior. Simply avoiding the table free/alloc solves this issue. BUG=b:135451288,chromium:941597 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -Wait for DHCP renewal, and see that v6 routes don't disappear. Change-Id: Ic2b2843599fe2612cf7801bb0aa515a58952480d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1674694 Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org>

shill: routing_table: Make protocol a part of RoutingTableEntry Prior to this change, all applied routes (added or deleted) used RTPROT_BOOT. However, certain routes use different protocols (IPv6 RA routes use RTPROT_RA, src route entries use RTPROT_KERNEL, etc). Since the RTPROT_* value was not parsed out of the RTNL message when listening for routing events, it was only possible to know of a route's protocol when the original RTNL message was still available. This change creates a protocol field as part of the RoutingTableEntry structure, such that parsed RoutingTableEntries contain the protocol value stored in the kernel table. Newly-created RoutingTableEntries use the RTPROT_BOOT protocol by default, which is also considered as a default protocol by `ip route add` and a number of kernel functions. BUG=chromium:930280,chromium:941597 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -IPv6 RA routes moved to per-device tables now correctly show that the routes are proto ra. tast: Introduce chromeos-base/tast-build-deps. This CL introduces the chromeos-base/tast-build-deps package where build time dependencies of all Tast related binaries (test runners and test bundles) are put. This package resolves a few problems about interaction between Portage and Tast: - Portage has a bug that --onlydeps-with-rdeps=n is ignored in a certain situation (https://bugs.gentoo.org/682472) and Tast had to work around the bug in a hacky and incomplete way when installing build time dependencies. The hack is no longer required after introduction of this package since the new package has no runtime-only dependency. - Formerly users were prompted to emerge dependencies even just after running update_chroot because local test dependencies were not installed to the host, adding tens of seconds to the runtime of the tast command. Now those dependencies are installed by update_chroot, so there is no need of additional emerge.
